headline: ARY does not have a seasonal business, it has a two-institution attendance business: for 27 days from about 26 December to 22 January the town empties and the till falls to exactly 35% of normal (both years, identically), and then one nine-day window (1-9 March) does 1.8x normal trade on the school-kit restock — so the whole year is won or lost by whether the uniform, footwear and winter-wear stock is landed in January and September rather than, as today, in the middle of the selling month.

findings.claim: Baru Sahib empties for a 27-day window each winter and the collapse is identical in both years measured: walk-in footfall falls to 35% of the pre-break norm, and the same 35% ratio appears in FY24-25 and FY25-26 independently.
findings.evidence: ary query: daily walk-in (CustomerID='00001') bills, 2025-11-15..2026-03-10 and 2024-12-15..2025-02-25. Full campus 15 Nov-23 Dec 2025 = 1,023 bills/day and Rs 1.42 L/day; 29 Dec-20 Jan = 357 bills/day and Rs 0.54 L/day. Prior year: ~780/day pre-break vs ~270/day in the trough.
findings.number: 357 vs 1,023 bills/day (35%); Rs 0.54 L vs Rs 1.42 L/day (38%); 27 days
findings.soWhat: Every January decision — roster, perishable ordering, cash, counting, receiving — should be built on a 35% number that is now proven and predictable, not guessed at each year.

findings.claim: The empty window is bounded by the two institutions' published breaks: Eternal University's winter break is 25 Dec - 31 Jan and the Akal Academies winter break starts around 24-26 Dec. The till shows the school returning on 21-25 Jan and the university on 1-3 Feb.
findings.evidence: https://eternaluniversity.edu.in/docs/AcademicCalendars2024-25.pdf (Winter break Dec 25, 2024 - Jan 31, 2025; even semester starts Feb 3; summer break Jul 1-30). Akal Academies Academic cum Activity Calendar 2024-25, https://bagha.akalacademy.ac.in/myadmin/cbse/CBSE_10-46-41.pdf (Winter Break 25/12-02/01; session ends mid-March; SESSION COMMENCES 24 March). Cross-checked against the daily till curve above.
findings.number: University break 38 days (25 Dec-31 Jan); Nursing college 30 Dec-25 Jan
findings.soWhat: The calendar is published months ahead and is not weather-dependent, so ARY can plan the trough to the day instead of reacting to it.

findings.claim: 1-9 March is the single biggest trading window of the year — 1,095 bills/day at Rs 2.53 L/day, i.e. 1.78x the full-campus norm — driven by the new school session's kit purchase, not by footfall.
findings.evidence: ary query: daily walk-in bills/value 2026-03-01..2026-03-09 vs 2025-11-15..2025-12-23. Basket index for March = 121 vs bills index 112 (FY-normalised, both years).
findings.number: Rs 2.53 L/day over 9 days; basket 21% above the yearly average
findings.soWhat: A stock-out on 1-9 March is the most expensive stock-out ARY can have, and it is a fixed, known date every year.

findings.claim: The school-kit season (Academy Dress, Footwear, Bags, Innerwear, Nightwear, Thermals) runs 20 Feb - 30 Apr and is worth Rs 42.9 lakh at retail, with 25% of it inside 9 days.
findings.evidence: ary query joining SaleDetail/SaleHeader/ProductMaster/ProductGroupMaster, daily 2026-02-15..2026-04-29, kit groups summed. Feb 20-28 Rs 3.46 L, March Rs 25.05 L, Apr 1-29 Rs 14.43 L.
findings.number: Rs 42.9 L over 70 days; Rs 10.6 L in 1-9 Mar
findings.soWhat: This is roughly 12% of the FY26-27 run-rate concentrated in one merchandising decision made in January.

findings.claim: ARY buys 20% of its uniform stock AFTER the season has opened. The FY26-27 kit was bought in two bills on 12 and 20 February plus Rs 2.37 lakh more on 4 and 26 March — and selling had already started on 20 February.
findings.evidence: ary query on PurchaseDetail/PurchaseHeader for ProductGroupName='Academy Dress', 2025-09-01 onward: 2026-02 Rs 9.48 L (2 bills, 12 and 20 Feb), 2026-03 Rs 2.37 L (2 bills, 4 and 26 Mar).
findings.number: Rs 2.37 L of Rs 11.85 L (20%) bought in-season
findings.soWhat: Chasing a fixed-date season is the classic stock-out signature; the fix costs nothing but a February purchase order moved into January.

findings.claim: Winter wear is bought inside its own selling peak, not ahead of it: Rs 9.56 lakh across 13 separate October bills (2-31 Oct) when the October selling index is already 199 and November is 264, plus Rs 1.61 lakh more as late as 26 January.
findings.evidence: ary query PurchaseDetail for 'Winter Wear': 2025-09 Rs 0.29 L, 2025-10 Rs 9.56 L / 13 bills, 2025-11 Rs 0.33 L, 2025-12 Rs 2.81 L, 2026-01 Rs 1.61 L. Sales index (FY-normalised, 2 yrs): Sep 63, Oct 199, Nov 264, Dec 204.
findings.number: 13 chase bills in one month; Rs 44.7 L/yr category (Winter Wear + Thermals)
findings.soWhat: Landing winter wear in September instead of October converts 13 panic reorders into one planned buy and protects the Oct-Dec run, the second-largest earning block of the year.

findings.claim: There are two separate back-to-campus waves with completely different baskets: the school's late-March session start buys clothing and footwear; the university's 1 August semester start buys household goods and stationery.
findings.evidence: FY-normalised category index (2 yrs, NGO bills excluded): Academy Dress Mar 347, Footwear Mar 210, Nightwear Mar 314, Bags Mar 246 vs House Hold Aug 210, Stationary Aug 204, Home Furnishing Jul 168, Accessories Aug 149. Eternal University odd semester begins 1 Aug with registration 2-8 Aug (academic calendar PDF).
findings.number: Mar clothing index 210-347; Aug household/stationery index 204-210
findings.soWhat: One 'back to school' plan is wrong — ARY needs a March apparel plan and a separate late-July household/stationery plan.

findings.claim: Adult apparel is a two-festival business, not a season: Womens Wear indexes 258 in April (Baisakhi) and 19 in November; Unstitched Suits peak in April (163) and October (162, Diwali) only.
findings.evidence: FY-normalised category index, resident bills only, 2 FYs. Womens Wear: Apr 258, May 190, Jun 230, Sep 54, Oct 31, Nov 19, Mar 20. Unstiched Suits: Apr 163, May 157, Jun 148, Oct 162, Jan 28, Feb 23.
findings.number: Womens Wear Apr 258 vs Nov 19 = 13x swing
findings.soWhat: Carrying adult apparel Sep-Feb ties up cash in the months ARY has least of it; buy it for two windows and clear it.

findings.claim: July is the second trough (sales index 89) but the inbound-goods collapse is far worse (purchase index 63, the year's low bar January) — and Sirmaur's roads are demonstrably closing in exactly that month.
findings.evidence: ary query PurchaseHeader monthly (IsDeleted=0) FY24-25 and FY25-26, FY-normalised. Jul purchase index 63 vs sales index 89; Oct 152 is the high. News evidence: 'Heavy rain shuts schools in Himachal's Sirmaur, Solan; MeT warns of flash floods, landslides' (New Indian Express, 10 Jul 2026); 'Red Alert For Kangra, Chamba And Sirmaur Districts' (ETV Bharat, 21 Jul 2026); 'over 200 roads still closed' (The Hindu, 14 Jul 2025).
findings.number: Jul purchase index 63 vs Jul sales index 89
findings.soWhat: Part of the July dip is ARY's own supply failing, not demand — which means a June buffer buys back sales rather than just insurance.

findings.claim: The monsoon window at Baru Sahib is tight and violent: July (292 mm, 26.5 rain days) and August (250 mm, 26.4 rain days) carry 47% of the annual 1,149 mm; median onset 13 June, median withdrawal 29 September.
findings.evidence: ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo archive API, lat 30.7549 lon 77.2957 (Baru Sahib, OSM/Nominatim), 2015-2024 daily, grid elevation 996 m; monthly normals and per-year onset (first 5-day total >=35 mm) / withdrawal (last 5-day total >=25 mm) computed locally.
findings.number: Jul 292 mm / 26.5 rain days; Aug 250 mm / 26.4; onset range 27 May - 5 Jul; withdrawal range 27 Aug - 4 Nov
findings.soWhat: For roughly 8 weeks it rains almost every day: umbrellas, footwear drying, damp-proof storage and a pre-built dry-grocery buffer are all June decisions.

findings.claim: The brief's altitude is wrong and it changes the winter plan: Baru Sahib sits at about 992-996 m, not ~1,700 m. There is no snow at the shop — zero modelled snow days in 10 years — but Rajgarh town on the ridge at 1,582 m averages 19 cm of snow over 7.5 days a year, 83% of it in January-February.
findings.evidence: PeakVisor POI 'Baru Sahib' = 992 m elevation, 30.754878N 77.295722E (https://peakvisor.com/poi/baru-sahib.html); Open-Meteo elevation API at the same point = 996 m; ERA5 snowfall_sum 2015-2024 = 0.0 cm every month at Baru Sahib vs 19.3 cm/yr and 7.5 snow days at 30.8807/77.3245 (Rajgarh, grid 1,582 m), min temp -7.4 C.
findings.number: 992 m (site) vs 1,582 m (Rajgarh ridge); 0 vs 7.5 snow days/yr
findings.soWhat: Sell cold-weather goods (thermals, blankets, heaters, hot drinks) but not snow goods; the snow risk is on the approach road, i.e. a January replenishment risk, not a January demand opportunity.

findings.claim: January is cold AND wet — it is the third-wettest month of the year (85 mm, 7.4 rain days) from western disturbances, while being the coldest (mean min 5.8 C, mean max 16.2 C).
findings.evidence: ERA5 monthly normals 2015-2024 at Baru Sahib (see above). Jan 84.7 mm, 7.4 days >=1 mm, 2.7 days >=10 mm; 10-year absolute minimum 0.2 C.
findings.number: Jan 85 mm vs Nov 11 mm and Dec 18 mm
findings.soWhat: The one month you cannot sell to residents is also the month the ridge road is least reliable — so the January kit landing has to be booked for the first half of the month, not the last week.

findings.claim: About 11-12% of ARY's turnover is NGO/institutional wholesale that has nothing to do with the Baru Sahib calendar: 'Hunger Heroes' (Delhi) takes one bill of Rs 5.5-6.9 lakh roughly monthly, and 'Katebaa Rural Services & Solutions Foundation' (Sonipat) Rs 8.4 lakh in 4 bills.
findings.evidence: ary query SaleHeader grouped by CustomerID, VoucherDate>='2025-09-01': 00001 walk-in Rs 5.48 Cr / 348,842 bills; 002CM Hunger Heroes Rs 70.6 L / 12 bills; 00240 Katebaa Rs 8.4 L / 4 bills. ary customers get 002CM / 00240.
findings.number: Rs 79 L over 16 bills in 12 months
findings.soWhat: Any seasonality read that includes these bills is distorted; separately, this is a Rs 79 L/yr wholesale line hiding inside a retail P&L and it is not seasonal at all — it may be the cleanest growth lever ARY has.

findings.claim: The physical stock count is already partly aligned to the troughs (27-30 Dec and mid-July) but uses only 4 days of the 27-day empty window — and the current count is being run on 21 August, a 110-index month.
findings.evidence: ary query PhysicalStockHeader by month and by day: Dec 2025 = 471 docs, all on 27-30 Dec; Jul 2025 = 814 docs concentrated 15-22 Jul; Aug 2026 = 114 docs, dated 21 Aug (ary audit counts shows counters Taran/Raunak/Audit-01 working 21 Aug 2026). Jan 2025 = 2 docs, Jan 2026 = 1 doc.
findings.number: 4 of 27 empty days used; 114 count docs on 21 Aug 2026
findings.soWhat: Against a lifetime physical-count shortage of Rs 2.59 Cr, counting a 357-bill/day shop for three weeks instead of a 1,100-bill/day shop for four days is free accuracy.

findings.claim: Perishables track the calendar exactly and are bought the same day they sell, so January over-ordering is pure wastage: Fruits index 47 in January (146 in June), Vegetable 71, Dairy 63, Bakery 46.
findings.evidence: FY-normalised category index, resident bills only, 2 FYs, sell vs buy side compared. Fruits sell index Apr 114/May 143/Jun 146/Jan 47 and buy index Apr 127/May 146/Jun 163/Jan 41 — buy and sell curves are within a few points every month.
findings.number: Fruits Jan 47 vs Jun 146
findings.soWhat: The ordering discipline on fresh is already good; the actionable part is a hard cut-off date (22 Dec) and restart date (20 Jan) so it does not have to be re-judged daily.

findings.claim: Thermals sell twice — November (index 244) and March (355) — because they are part of the returning students' kit, not only a winter purchase. But they are bought in September-October and again in mid-January, i.e. never for the March peak.
findings.evidence: Sell index (2 FYs): Sep 86, Oct 176, Nov 244, Dec 147, Mar 355, Jun 6. Purchases: 23 Sep 2025 Rs 1.52 L, Oct Rs 0.74 L, 15-26 Jan 2026 Rs 0.71 L, 26 Feb Rs 0.03 L.
findings.number: March index 355, the highest single month for any winter line
findings.soWhat: March thermal demand is being served out of leftover November stock — which is exactly why some of it is bought in January at the wrong end of the season.

findings.claim: Uniform FABRIC is bought while the town is empty (January index 96-227 against a February index of 36) — someone is already using the empty window to buy cloth for the March session. That instinct is correct and is not applied to any other category.
findings.evidence: FY-normalised index for group 'Fabrics': all-customer view Jan 227/Feb 27; resident-only view Jan 96/Feb 36/Mar 139/Apr 133.
findings.number: Fabrics Jan index up to 227
findings.soWhat: The January-buy discipline exists inside ARY already; the recommendation is to extend it from cloth to the whole kit rather than introduce a new behaviour.

findings.claim: Ary Clothing is a two-month business: March index 292 and April 173 against December 24 and February 53. Ary Pos (main grocery) is far steadier but still halves in January (56).
findings.evidence: ary query SaleDetail x WarehouseMaster, FY25-26 (2025-04-01..2026-04-01), value index per counter. Ary Pos Rs 415.9 L (Jan 56, Feb 66, Oct 133); Ary Clothing Rs 139.8 L (Mar 292, Apr 173, Dec 24); G Canteen Rs 46.9 L (Oct 151, Jan 52); Fruits & Veg Rs 42.8 L (Aug 150, Jan 64).
findings.number: Ary Clothing Mar 292 vs Dec 24 = 12x
findings.soWhat: Staffing and shelf space at Ary Clothing should flex 12x across the year; a fixed roster there is a year-round cost against a two-month revenue.

findings.claim: ARY carries 288 'Academy Books' SKUs and has sold Rs 100 of books in 29 months. The school's book demand is not going through ARY at all.
findings.evidence: ary masters product-groups: group 181 Academy Books, subgroup Books, 288 SKUs. ary query SaleDetail joined to ProductGroupMaster for 'Academy Books', VoucherDate>='2024-04-01': one row, 2024-04, Rs 100.
findings.number: 288 SKUs, Rs 100 of sales since Apr 2024
findings.soWhat: Either the biggest un-served April category in the town (5,000 students' books) or 288 dead SKUs cluttering the catalogue — worth one phone call to the academy office to find out which.

findings.claim: The purchase calendar peaks in October (index 152) and February (117) — so the two big buying decisions of ARY's year are already made in those months. Both are one month later than they should be.
findings.evidence: ary query PurchaseHeader monthly, FY-normalised, FY24-25 + FY25-26: Apr 116, May 130, Jun 119, Jul 63, Aug 98, Sep 108, Oct 152, Nov 73, Dec 84, Jan 59, Feb 117, Mar 84.
findings.number: Oct 152 and Feb 117 are the two buying peaks
findings.soWhat: This is a shift-left problem, not a new-process problem: move the October buy to September and the February buy to January and the rest of the calendar already works.

findings.claim: Suppliers are almost all within a day's road of Baru Sahib (HP state code 02, plus Chandigarh 04, Haryana 06, Delhi 07), so 'a month early' is a cash and planning decision, not a logistics one.
findings.evidence: ary purchases by-supplier --from 2025-09-01 --to 2026-08-21: top suppliers Shashi Bhushan Manoj Kumar Aeron (Rs 65.1 L, no GSTIN), Dharam Pal & Sons 04AAKFD..., Himachal Wholesale Syndicate 02AABFH..., Raja Ram Jai Prakash 02AAEFR..., Solan Agencies 02AERPS..., Lakhmi Chand Tejoo Mal 07AAAFL..., Gupta Textile 06ACKPK...
findings.number: 9 of the top 15 suppliers are HP (02)
findings.soWhat: There is no transit excuse for landing stock late; the binding constraint is January cash, which is the month with the lowest collections.

findings.claim: The festival calendar is fixed and known for the next 18 months, and the two on-campus samagams (Sant Attar Singh, around 18 Feb; Sant Teja Singh, around 5 Jul) fall in ARY's two weakest windows.
findings.evidence: Festival dates from https://www.officeholidays.com/countries/india/2026 and /2027 (Diwali 8 Nov 2026 and 29 Oct 2027; Guru Nanak's Birthday 24 Nov 2026 and 13 Nov 2027; Parkash Gurpurab Guru Gobind Singh 28 Dec 2026; Dussehra 20-21 Oct 2026, 9 Oct 2027; Raksha Bandhan 28 Aug 2026, 17 Aug 2027; Holi 22 Mar 2027; Vaisakhi 14 Apr 2027; Guru Ravidas 20 Feb 2027; HP Statehood Day 25 Jan; Himachal Day 15 Apr). Nanakshahi fixed dates from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanakshahi_calendar. Samagam dates from the Akal Academies 2024-25 calendar (Sant Attar Singh Sant Samagam 18 Feb; Sant Teja Singh Sant Samagam 5 Jul).
findings.number: Diwali 8 Nov 2026; Gurpurab 24 Nov 2026; Baisakhi 14 Apr 2027; Hola Mohalla 23 Mar 2027
findings.soWhat: A samagam brings outside visitors into a month running at 71 (Feb) and 89 (Jul) of index — the only demand ARY can add to its two weak months without waiting for students to come back.

findings.claim: Roughly 60-65% of ARY's customer base are boarders who leave; the residual January population is about 1,500-2,000 people (staff, married staff families, local villagers).
findings.evidence: Derived: 357 walk-in bills/day in the empty window vs 1,023 in the full-campus window, applied to the stated ~5,000 residents. Not confirmed against any headcount roll from the Trust.
findings.number: ~1,750 residual residents (range 1,500-2,000)
findings.soWhat: A shop sized and staffed for 5,000 is serving 1,750 for a month — and that residual group is the only year-round, weather-proof customer base ARY has.

findings.claim: Akal Academy's own vacation notification for the Baru Sahib campus was never obtained; the school half of the empty window is inferred from the till, and the only calendar found is the trust-wide 2024-25 activity calendar hosted on the Bagha (Punjab) academy site.
findings.evidence: Searched and fetched: barusahib.org (no events/calendar page, /events/ returns 404), eternaluniversity.edu.in/Academics (only the 2024-25 calendar PDF is linked; 2025-26 and 2026-27 return HTTP 404), bagha.akalacademy.ac.in activity calendar 2024-25. WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted at 200 calls.
findings.soWhat: If the Baru Sahib campus shifts its winter break by a fortnight, the January plan moves with it — one email to the academy office removes the only soft joint in this whole calendar.

recommendations.action: Move the entire school-kit purchase into the first half of January and require every kit line — uniforms, footwear, bags, innerwear, nightwear, thermals — to be received, priced and on the floor by 5 February. Today the season opens on 20 February with only one of two purchase bills landed, and 20% of the Academy Dress buy (Rs 2.37 L at cost) is made in March, inside the peak. The season is worth Rs 42.9 L retail with 25% of it in nine days, so even a 10% stock-out recovery is Rs 4-5 L/yr. ESTIMATED impact.
recommendations.blocker: January is the lowest-collection month of the year (walk-in Rs 22.2 L vs a Rs 43.4 L average), so the buy needs either a short January credit line or February-dated supplier bills against January delivery. Agree that with the top three apparel suppliers first.

recommendations.action: Shift the winter-wear and thermals buy one month left: order in August, land by 20 September, one planned tranche instead of 13 October chase bills. Today Rs 9.56 L arrives across 13 bills spread through October while October already sells at index 199 and November at 264 — and Rs 1.61 L is still being bought on 26 January, at the wrong end of the season. Winter Wear + Thermals is Rs 44.7 L/yr. ESTIMATED impact of Rs 3-5 L/yr recovered plus less end-of-season markdown.
recommendations.blocker: none — the same HP/Delhi suppliers are already used; this is a purchase-order date change.

recommendations.action: Build an explicit monsoon buffer every June: 4-6 weeks of dry grocery, atta, oil, sugar, toiletries and umbrellas landed by 10 June. July inbound purchases fall to index 63 (the year's low bar January) against July sales of 89, and Sirmaur roads are documented closing in exactly that month, so part of the July dip is ARY's own supply failing rather than demand.
recommendations.blocker: Storage space and the working capital to hold six weeks of dry goods through the wettest month — quantify the shelf/godown capacity at Baru Sahib before committing the order.

recommendations.action: Turn the 27-day empty window (approximately 26 December to 22 January) into a scheduled operating reset: full physical count across all counters, planogram and shelf reset, kit receiving and ticketing, and staff leave. They currently use only 4 days of it (27-30 December, 471 count documents) and are instead counting on 21 August, a 110-index month. Against a lifetime physical-count shortage of Rs 2.59 Cr, counting a 357-bill/day shop for three weeks instead of an 1,100-bill/day shop for four days is free accuracy.
recommendations.blocker: Staff want their own leave in the same window — split the team into a count crew and a leave crew and publish the rota in November.

recommendations.action: Publish a hard perishable cut-off of 22 December and a restart of 20 January, and cut the fresh order to 35% for the window. Fruits fall to index 47, Bakery 46, Dairy 63 and Vegetable 71 in January, and these lines are bought the same day they sell, so every day of un-cut ordering is wastage.
recommendations.blocker: none — this is a standing instruction to the Fruits & Veg and Ary Pos counters. The Rs figure is ESTIMATED from the January index gap on perishable groups, not from a measured wastage log.

recommendations.action: Merchandise two named baskets on fixed dates: the GOING-HOME basket for 18-24 December (gifts, sweets, dry fruit, travel bags, warm clothes for the journey) and the COMING-BACK basket for 21-31 January and 1-3 February (toiletries, stationery, snacks, bedding). Both edges of the empty window are currently unmerchandised, and the 24-25 December days already show the largest baskets of the winter.
recommendations.blocker: none. ESTIMATED impact — no basket-level test has been run, so treat this as a hypothesis to measure in December 2026 against December 2025's daily curve.

recommendations.action: Make adult apparel a two-window buy — Baisakhi (land by 5 April) and Diwali (land by 25 October) — and stop carrying Womens Wear, Mens Wear and Unstitched Suits through September-February. Womens Wear runs at index 258 in April and 19 in November; Unstitched Suits 163 in April, 162 in October, 23 in February.
recommendations.blocker: Somebody must own the clear-out: agree a markdown ladder for unsold festive apparel in the second week after each festival, otherwise the stock simply carries.

recommendations.action: Flex the Ary Clothing counter's roster and floor space to its calendar: index 292 in March and 173 in April against 24 in December and 53 in February. A fixed year-round roster there is a 12-month cost against a 2-month revenue.
recommendations.blocker: Staff are Trust employees rather than seasonal hires, so the flex has to be redeployment to Ary Pos in the low months, not headcount reduction. Confirm that is allowed before planning it.

recommendations.action: Settle the Academy Books question with one call to the academy office: 288 book SKUs are catalogued and have produced Rs 100 of sales in 29 months, in a town with roughly 5,000 students. Either win the book and workbook supply for the March-April session, or delist all 288 SKUs so they stop polluting the catalogue and the count.
recommendations.blocker: Unknown whether the Trust supplies textbooks free or centrally — that answer decides which of the two actions applies.

recommendations.action: Treat the NGO/wholesale line as a separate business with its own plan: Hunger Heroes (Delhi) and Katebaa Rural Services (Sonipat) bought Rs 79 lakh across 16 bills in the last 12 months, roughly 11-12% of turnover, and it is completely independent of the resident calendar. It is the only revenue ARY can grow in January.
recommendations.blocker: Nobody has confirmed whether these are contracted programmes or opportunistic orders; ask the Baru Sahib counter manager who places them and on what cycle.

recommendations.action: Fix the two data blindnesses that stop this calendar from getting sharper: 97% of bills sit on one walk-in account (00001) and 99.7% carry no SalesPersonID, so ARY cannot see WHICH customers disappear in January or who sells the kit season. A staff/student/family flag on the walk-in till, even three buttons, would turn the 35% trough into a named segment.
recommendations.blocker: FusionERP8 POS configuration — check whether the till can capture a customer type without slowing the queue at 1,095 bills/day.

openQuestions: Akal Academy Baru Sahib's own dated vacation notification for the current session was never obtained — barusahib.org has no calendar or events page (/events/ returns 404) and the only Akal calendar found is the trust-wide 2024-25 document hosted on the Bagha (Punjab) academy site. The Principal's or Registrar's office at Baru Sahib can supply it in one email, and it is the single soft joint in this whole plan.

Eternal University's 2025-26 and 2026-27 academic calendars are not published (only 2024-25 is linked from /Academics; the obvious 2025-26 and 2026-27 PDF paths return HTTP 404). Confirm with the Controller of Examinations whether winter break is still 25 Dec - 31 Jan and summer break 1-30 Jul, because both dates anchor the trough.

Headcount split: how many of the ~5,000 residents are boarders who leave, versus staff, married staff families and day scholars who stay? The till says roughly 60-65% leave, but that is derived from bill counts, not from a roll. The Kalgidhar Trust admin office has the number.

Does the ridge road through Rajgarh (1,582 m) actually close for snow or ice in January? ERA5 says ~10 cm of snow over 3-4 days there, but reanalysis at 996 m grid resolution cannot see a single blocked hairpin. The local transporter or the counter manager knows how many delivery days were lost last January.
Who supplies the academy's textbooks and workbooks, and is that contract available? 288 book SKUs with Rs 100 of sales in 29 months is either the town's biggest unserved category or 288 dead records.

Are Hunger Heroes (Rs 70.6 L / 12 bills) and Katebaa Rural Services (Rs 8.4 L / 4 bills) contracted CSR feeding programmes on a fixed cycle, or opportunistic? If contracted, this is a Rs 79 L/yr counter-cyclical line that could be grown in exactly the months the town is empty.

What actually drives the March Winter Wear index of 178 — returning students buying warm clothes for cold March nights, or end-of-season clearance of October's over-buy? The answer decides whether to hold winter stock through March or mark it down in January. A margin check on March winter-wear lines would settle it.

The Basement counter shows zero sales in November and March and 11 in January/February in FY25-26, which looks like an opening/closing artifact rather than seasonality. Confirm with the counter manager before using Basement numbers for anything.

Whether the Akal Academy Baru Sahib campus takes any June break at all: the trust-wide calendar shows SUMMER BREAK 1-30 June for the academies, yet ARY's June index is 119 (the third-highest month). Either Baru Sahib is exempt as a winter-closing hill campus, or the June population is staff and university students only — worth confirming, because a June emptying would change the monsoon-buffer plan.
confidenceGap: The internal seasonality is as solid as it gets — two full independent fiscal years of day-level till data, the same 35% trough ratio and the same 27-day window in both, cross-checked against the published Eternal University and Akal Academies calendars. What stops it being certain is that I never read Akal Academy Baru Sahib's OWN dated vacation notification: the school half of the empty window (roughly 26 Dec to 22 Jan) is inferred from the till, and the only Akal calendar I could obtain is the trust-wide 2024-25 document hosted on the Bagha, Punjab academy site, which shows a plains pattern (a short 25 Dec - 2 Jan winter break and a full June summer break) that ARY's own data flatly contradicts for Baru Sahib. If the Baru Sahib campus shifts its winter break by a fortnight, the January kit-landing deadline and the count window move with it. Secondary gap: the climate figures are ERA5 reanalysis on a 996 m grid cell, not an IMD station at the campus, so treat the temperature extremes and the "no snow at the shop" claim as model-derived — directionally reliable, but a cold valley night can go several degrees below what the grid reports.
